newsitem.title: UK: Sneeze-injured Briton plucked from Himalaya peak.
newsitem.headline: Sneeze-injured Briton plucked from Himalaya peak.

text.p: A British climber was airlifted off a Himalayan mountainside in Pakistan on Monday after spending a week immobilised with a back injury suffered from a sneeze.
Alan Hinkes pulled a muscle when the flour dusting from a chapati, thin unleavened bread, went up his nose and caused him to sneeze violently.

"It's amazing that something as trivial as eating a chapati could have landed me in such trouble," Hinkes said in a statement faxed to his sponsors in Britain from his hospital bed in Islamabad. "I've spent more than a week in absolute agony and wondered if I was ever going to get off that mountain."

Hinkes was able to call emergency rescuers after his injury at 13,000 feet (4,000 metres) on Nanga Parbat, known locally as the Killer Mountain, with a satellite telephone, but poor weather kept a rescue effort grounded.
He spent the week with a short supply of food and pain killers. Armed locals also robbed him of vital equipment.
Hinkes, who was attempting to climb the world's 14 highest peaks and has already reached the summit of nine of them, intends to resume climbing after his recovery.
